title: New Old Crocodile Is Missing Its Nose Tip, Just Like the Sphinx
summary:
The Great Sphinx in Egypt is famous for its missing nose. Now scientists have named a new kind of extinct crocodile. Its fossil skull is missing the tip of its snout, too!

The new species is called Herugavialis cairensis. It was a gavial, a crocodile with a long, thin snout. Only two kinds of gavials are alive today. But long ago, they lived all over the world.

The skull was dug up in the 1920s from a 45-million-year-old layer of rock in Egypt. At first, scientists thought it was a crocodile kind that is still alive today. New tools helped them look inside the skull. They found it was a new species.

"We decided to name the new crocodile after the Egyptian god Heru," said scientist Philip Mannion. Crocodiles disappeared from the Mediterranean area when that sea dried up about 6 million years ago.
why_it_matters: It shows that old fossils in museums can still hold new surprises for curious scientists.
